peer_research_diagnostics.JARVIS_to_MOTIF: More sensors, routes or code are not proof of better field outcomes. Preserve the transparent persistence control and an ability to abstain.
peer_research_diagnostics.MOTIF_to_JARVIS: A method that wins on one validation block can fail under different physical conditions. Respect sealed event error and sensor availability.
peer_research_diagnostics.next_experiment: Choose an entirely different future or independently archived flood event and freeze this policy unchanged before access to target labels.
peer_research_diagnostics.self_critique: This preselected 2024 flood is a single historical event. Missing upstream sensors, report-time hindsight, later ratings and a conservative rule invented after 016 failure undermine generalization.

source_limitations: 2024 flood was selected retrospectively from documented historical events; not sampled randomly.
The 2024 Rapidan dam event temporarily disrupted gauge power; missingness is informative and can bias results.
Raw USGS API source captures in run artifact can change if re-fetched after later station revisions.
No original time-of-issue telemetry snapshots, rating curves or independent verification of physical outcomes.
Models calibrated on 2023/early-2024 history, not modern official flood forecast tools.
No stage thresholds, warnings, contacts, evacuation, safety advice or real-world decisions.
A win over a weak historical policy is not proof of generally improved intelligence.
